survey-aim-scope: Abstract, p.1: the authors state the survey objective and near-term focus in their own words.
survey-reimplementation: Abstract, p.1: the authors state they re-implemented methods, built the hybrid transformer and applied QSA and QRNN to NLP; the paper's own scope.
qnn-pipeline-definition: Section II, p.2: the three-step QNN pipeline and the even/odd parity readout for binary classification are described as the setting the paper uses.
qrnn-encoding-angle: Section III, p.2: QRNN input x(t) in [0,1] is embedded by RY angles equal to the inverse cosine of the input, as stated with Fig. 1.
qrnn-text-experiment-setup: Section IV.B, p.3: datasets MC, RP, Amazon, Yelp, IMDB, TF-IDF vectorization, 200 epochs and learning rate 0.08 are stated in one passage.
qsal-architecture-definition: Section V.B, p.4: QSAL is described as a quantum circuit part with Uq, Uk, Uv sharing one ansatz and a classical post-processing part.
qsal-gaussian-attention: Section V.B, p.4, eq. (1) and the text after it: Gaussian projected attention, its normalization and the weighted sum of value vectors are defined. The method is adopted from [30] but is the model the paper runs.
qsann-text-setup: Section V.C, p.4 to p.5: four-word sentences, extension to a 6-length vector with two zeros, D=2, one QSAL layer and learning rate 0.005 are stated for both tasks.
positional-encoding-setup: Section V.E, p.5: embedding layer, positional encoding layer, embedding dimension 2, 2 text pieces, D=2, nq=2, learning rate 0.005 are stated.
qsann-dataset-size: Section V.C, p.5: 'RP task has 74 training samples (containing 91 words) and 31 test samples' is in the passage (the sentence starts on p.4 with the MC task).
qsann-near-term-scope: Section V.B, p.4: the authors say that, because of near-term simulator and hardware limits, they focus on the several-variational-circuits model with classical post-processing; the value matches.
chen-2024-vqe-definition: Section I, p.1, eq. (1): VQE is defined with its loss L(theta) equal to the Hamiltonian expectation; the minimum state is 'approximately the ground state'.
vqd-ssvqe-definitions: Section I, p.1: both methods are described in the paper's words (VQD adds fidelity penalty; SSVQE sums orthogonal-state energies for one optimization). These are the two methods the paper compares.
vqd-method-details: Section II.B.2, p.2 to p.3, eq. (8) and Fig. 2: separate unitaries per state, sequential optimization of eq. (8), and the swap test or unitary-inversion overlap are described.
fs-vqe-definition: Section II.B.3, p.3, eq. (9): H' = (H - omega)^2 maps states near omega to the ground state; FS-VQE is a normal VQE on H'.
se-ansatz-unphysical-states: Section II.C.3, p.4: the authors state the SE ansatz does not conserve spin and charge so excited energies are unphysical without a constraint. Section III.C, p.6 to p.7: they add the Sz constraint with mz=0. Limit and fix are in the paper.
qubit-tapering-definition: Section II.D, p.4: qubit tapering is defined as omitting qubits acted on by at most one Pauli operator, substituting eigenvalues +/-1.
lih-resource-setup: Section III.A, p.5: LiH has 6 orbitals, 2 qubits each, 12 qubits; the 99.9% accuracy test by exact diagonalization is stated.
optimizer-comparison-setup: Section III.B, p.6: FS-VQE on LiH, learning rate 0.07, 1.6 angstrom, omega -7.8 Ha, three layers spin-restricted QCCSD, zero initialization, stop at threshold or 400th iteration are stated (threshold is 10^-6; the value leaves it unnamed, which is accurate).
comparison-vqd-ssvqe-setup: Section III.C, p.6: QCCSD, Adam, learning rate 0.3, identical initial states, VQD layers 2/3/4, SSVQE 4 layers, threshold 10^-5 are all stated.
h4-test-setup: Section III.D, p.7 to p.8: H4 with 8 qubits, target near -1.0 Ha, lr 0.3, beta 5, wj 0.4, 5 QCCSD layers, zero start, threshold 10^-5 are stated.
chen2024-scope-larger-molecules: Abstract p.1: the study compares VQD and SSVQE for low-lying LiH excited states. Section IV, p.9: it states studying larger molecules is crucial and left for future work. Both are the paper's own scope statements.
defi-study-aim: Abstract, p.1: the authors state the study is an empirical QML vs CML comparison on AMM and DeFi strategies by backtesting 10 models on crypto assets.
defi-dataset-setup: Section III.A.1, p.2: assets BTCUSDC, ETHUSDC, USDCUSDT, daily data, 252 trading days, 2024-01-01 to 2025-01-01. Table VIII, p.12 gives the end date as 2024-12-31 (minor internal difference).
defi-task-definition: Section III.B, p.2: y in {0,1} marks whether rebalancing should occur; tau_rebalance=0.02 and tau_price=0.01 are stated in the text. Eq. (2) is scrambled in the text layer; the value rests on the thresholds in the prose, not on the equation form.
defi-data-split: Section III.D, p.4 (eqs. 48 to 50) and Section VI.A, p.11: time-ordered 70/15/15 split to avoid leakage.
defi-feature-counts: Section VI.A, p.11 and Table I, p.3: 50-80 classical and 6-8 quantum features; Appendix, p.12: states 122 classical features. The paper is inconsistent (its appendix categories sum to 110, not 122), but the value reports both statements as the paper makes them.
defi-quantum-feature-encoding: Section III.C.2, p.3 to p.4, eq. (41) and eqs. (42) to (47): min-max scaling times 2 pi, six qubits with feature pairs from feature importance.
defi-model-groups: Abstract p.1 and Table I p.3: groups and counts 3/3/3/1 as stated; Table III lists one Transformer.
defi-model-hyperparameters: Appendix D, p.12: VQE Classifier 6 qubits, 2 layers, Adam lr 0.01; QNN 6 qubits, 3 layers; QSVM RBF kernel, as stated.
defi-hybrid-model-definitions: Sections III.G and III.H, p.4 to p.5: QASA via VQCs, QRWKV with quantum evolution, and the Hybrid vs Sequence input difference (features vs 10 time steps) are stated as the models tested.
defi-hybrid-model-settings: Appendix E, p.12: QASA Hybrid 12 features, 2 quantum layers, 1 classical layer; QASA Sequence LSTM 64 units, 2 quantum layers, dropout 0.2.
defi-runs-and-experiments: Section VI.A, p.11 and Table VIII, p.12: 10 models, 5 runs each, 50 experiments.
defi-stated-limitations-model-compute: Section V.C, p.11: both limitations are listed by the authors as research limitations of their work.
defi-limitations-crypto-only: Section V.C, p.11: 'Study based only on cryptocurrency data; results may not apply to other financial markets.' Section VI.A, p.11: three crypto asset pairs.
adaboostq-weak-classifier-definition: Main text, p.1 to p.2: the ensemble and AdaBoost description (weak classifiers, sequential training, sample weights for attention) is the base the paper builds on, in the paper's words.
adaboostq-classifier-readout-definition: Main text, p.2: m measured qubits, PVM divided equally into K groups, class k if the state is in group k, and P as confidence.
adaboostq-weight-update-rule: Main text, p.2, eq. (1) and Algorithm 1, p.7: w_{l+1,i} = w_{l,i}/Z * exp[P(1 - 2 delta)], initial weights 1/N, normalizer Z. The text layer is readable here and matches the algorithm box.
adaboostq-classifier-weight-and-cl: Main text, p.2, eq. (3) and Algorithm 1, p.7: alpha_l = ln(c_l P_true / P_false), c_l default 1, tuned in practice (Algorithm 1 sets c_l by argmax of training accuracy).
adaboostq-loss-function: Main text, p.2, eq. (2): L_{l,b} = -w ln P_{y_b}, summed over a batch.
adaboostq-ensemble-rule: Main text, p.2, eq. (4): label is argmax over k of the sum of alpha_l P_k; matches Algorithm 1.
adaboostq-device-description: Main text, p.2 to p.3: 11x11 frequency-tunable transmons with tunable couplers, native single-qubit and CZ gates, median Pauli errors about 5e-4 and 6e-3.
adaboostq-mnist-setup: Main text, p.3 and Fig. 2 caption: ten-qubit chain, 30 trainable parameters, 3,600 images of 28x28 (360 per digit), two parallel QNN copies, trainable matrix W.
adaboostq-mnist-data-selection: Methods, p.6: k-means selects 3,600 images, test set is all 10,000 MNIST test images, 1,000 random test images (100 per digit) monitor accuracy.
adaboostq-qcnn-setup: Main text p.4 and Fig. 4 caption p.5: 15-qubit 1D chain, directly implementable gates, three conv/pool rounds, CZ fully connected layer, 45 variational parameters.
adaboostq-qcnn-task-and-data: Main text p.4 and Methods p.6: three-phase cluster-Ising classification, 2,204 training and 1,564 test states, test regime larger than training regime to test generalization.
adaboostq-qcnn-states-prepared-by-vqc: Main text p.4, Methods p.6, Supplement p.11: states prepared by VQCs trained classically, then run on the processor; energies within 1.8% above ground state as stated in the data-preparation supplement.
adaboostq-qcnn-discarded-critical-points: Supplement, p.10 to p.11: parameter sets failing 10 retries are discarded, usually near critical points. The authors state this as a coverage limit of their dataset.
adaboostq-qcnn-training-procedure: Methods p.6 and Algorithm 3 p.8: 5 epochs, 76 batches of 29 states (76 x 29 = 2,204), init in [-pi, pi), finite difference (epsilon 0.2), Adam rate 0.02.
adaboostq-data-availability: Data and Code availability, p.5: both are stated as 'will be made publicly available upon publication', so not yet available in this version (v1, March 2025). The value says exactly this.
adaboostq-hardware-setup: Main text p.2 to p.3: 'fully programmable superconducting quantum processor [12]' and a 15-qubit 1D QCNN chain, both stated in the setup passage (the first sentence ends p.2).
uav-study-scope: Abstract, p.1: three QML approaches vs classical baselines, 8-feature input, identical preprocessing, balancing and noise-model assumptions, as stated.
uav-dataset-description: Section III.A, p.4: UAVIDS-2025, NS-3.24, extended BOID, Nakagami, 802.11ac, AODV, 21 features per flow. Note the next paragraph says 22 raw attributes (internal inconsistency; the value reports the 21 stated).
uav-feature-engineering: Section III.A, p.4: 22 raw attributes distilled to 8 features, log(1+x) on rp, rb, PMR, standardization with training-only statistics are stated.
uav-balanced-subset: Introduction, p.2: the authors state they build a balanced subset, evaluate each approach, and compare accuracy, robustness and resource cost against SVM baselines. The abstract also names CNN baselines, so the value is partial but not wrong.
uav-qtnn-definition: Section II.D, p.3 to p.4: QT-NN is defined as a circuit producing classical weights through a mapping T, with input-independent circuit and end-to-end training.
uav-simulation-and-data-availability: Data availability, p.5: the dataset is public as described in [38] and tensor-network simulations used cuTN-QSVM; abstract p.1 says code and partitions are released.
uav-simulated-data-no-hardware: Abstract p.1, Section III.A p.4, Section IV p.5: the data are an NS-3 simulation corpus of 122,171 records in five categories (Normal plus four attacks), and real hardware runs are future work. The stored 'five attack types' conflicts with the body (four attack types plus Normal), so the reader's correction is right. Scope statement.
